text.p: Mexican cement producer Cemex's 12.75 percent Eurobonds due 2006 are the cheapest of the company's assets and should trade 25 basis points tighter than at current levels, Salomon Brothers said in a report released on Thursday.
"We believe that Cemex's strategy to improve the firm's credit fundamentals ahead of any major expansion activity is prudent," Salomon Brothers said.
It said Cemex is exploring the possibility of creating a committed backstop facility through a group of banks in an effort to mitigate refinancing risk.
"We recommend the ICA 2001 Eurobonds at an offer spread of 296 basis points over U.S. Treasuries," Salomon said.
The company said construction company Empresas ICA's 2001 notes should trade at about 40 basis points wider than the Cemex 2001 notes.

It added that investors concerned about Mexico's presidential elections in 2000 should look at ICA's 9.75 percent Eurobonds due 1998 at 213 basis points over U.S. Treasuries and at Bufete Industrial's 11.375 percent Eurobonds due 1999 at 267 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
"The true upside to Bufete noteholders will reside in Bufete's realization of the overdue receivables from the CFE (Commission Federal de Electricidad)," said Salomon.

It said ICA's credit profile stands to improve on its ability to monetize its equity investments in Mexico's toll road system as well as receive payments from the government for construction work it had performed.
